memory_update.text: New Hotspots should be treated as a meta-theme: use breaking supply shocks and policy shifts to identify second-order bottlenecks rather than starting with popular tickers.
AI infrastructure decomposition should include underfollowed passive components and advanced substrate materials, not only GPUs, HBM, networking, and power equipment.
Critical-minerals processing may be constrained by sulphur and sulphuric-acid availability, creating a reagent/logistics chokepoint worth separate public-market mapping.
Niche API suppliers with regulatory re-validation lock-in are a separate hidden-supplier lane for healthcare supply-chain diversification themes.
Layer 1B should verify ticker-level exposure through filings, capacity data, customer qualification, regulatory documents, and segment financials before ranking companies.

layer1a.summary: Layer 1A decomposes 'New Hotspots' into six concrete chokepoint lanes where breaking news, policy shifts, supply shocks, or second-order AI/electrification demand could expose underfollowed public-market beneficiaries. The highest-quality decomposition is not a single-ticker map; it is a cross-sector funnel spanning AI infrastructure materials, power-electronics components, critical-minerals processing inputs, niche pharmaceutical APIs, automotive aluminum rolling, and nuclear-fuel / reactor-supply dependencies. Several nodes are deliberately one or two steps away from obvious mega-cap demand drivers, making them suitable for small/mid-cap discovery in later layers.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: The bottleneck is not the overall MLCC market but a narrow high-end band requiring small size, high capacitance, low ESR, and low ESL, where only a few global suppliers may be qualified for mass production.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Prioritize USD 1B-15B component makers with segment exposure to high-end MLCCs, power inductors, or advanced passive components; include larger leaders only as reference comps.
supply_chain_nodes.node: High-end AI-server MLCCs and board-level passive components
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Use Murata and other large passive-component leaders as reference anchors, then search for smaller Japanese, Korean, Taiwanese, and specialty passive-component suppliers with AI-server exposure, high-end product mix, or capacity-expansion evidence.
search_queries: "high capacitance" "low ESL" MLCC data center supplier
supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: The market may focus on GPUs, HBM, and networking while missing passive components whose unit demand scales dramatically with each AI server rack.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: AI accelerators and high-density server boards require large volumes of high-performance capacitors to stabilize power delivery, reduce impedance, and support rapid current draw near GPUs and accelerators.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: Process know-how, glass chemistry, weaving tolerances, and multi-year qualification cycles may create a concentrated supplier base that is hard to replicate quickly with capital alone.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Look for Japanese, Taiwanese, Korean, and European specialty-material companies in the USD 500M-10B range with high-margin advanced materials segments and capacity additions in 2026-2027.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Advanced glass / T-glass for high-speed AI substrates
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Map the dominant advanced-glass supplier as a reference leader, then search adjacent substrate, laminate, glass-fiber, specialty-material, and PCB material suppliers with AI-server or high-speed networking qualifications.
search_queries: "glass fiber" "low dielectric" data center AI supplier
"high speed" PCB material "AI server" listed company
supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: This node sits below visible AI chip and server demand; obscure material suppliers may capture pricing power before broader investors connect them to AI infrastructure.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: Advanced glass materials can become hidden enablers for high-speed AI electronics where signal integrity, substrate performance, and manufacturing tolerances matter.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: A simultaneous policy and logistics shock can force Chilean copper producers, Indonesian HPAL nickel operators, and fertilizer users to compete for limited replacement acid and sulphur volumes, creating second-order winners in logistics, smelter acid, sulphur supply, and substitution routes.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Prioritize regional chemical, fertilizer, smelting, logistics, and industrial-gas/acid companies between USD 300M-10B; treat small chemical distributors as speculative-shadow candidates until filings confirm exposure.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Sulphur and sulphuric-acid supply for copper, nickel HPAL, and fertilizers
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Search beyond miners into sulphur producers, smelter operators with acid byproduct, shipping/logistics firms, fertilizer producers, and regional chemical distributors with route optionality.
search_queries: "sulphur" export ban beneficiary fertilizer chemical company
supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: The visible story is copper/nickel scarcity, but the investable chokepoint may be the reagent and trade-route layer that determines whether processing assets can operate economically.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: Sulphuric acid is a critical reagent for copper SX-EW, HPAL nickel processing, fertilizers, and industrial acid markets, so trade disruptions can cascade into electrification and battery supply chains.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: Specialty API manufacturers with approved molecules, long-term customer relationships, and non-China sourcing appeal can gain pricing power and durable revenue as global pharma diversifies supplier bases.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Prioritize USD 300M-5B listed specialty API makers with high EBITDA margins, low analyst coverage, and molecule-level catalysts; avoid assuming customer names without filing confirmation.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Niche pharmaceutical API suppliers with regulatory re-validation lock-in
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Search Indian and other non-China listed API manufacturers by molecule portfolio, DMF filings, USFDA/EU inspection status, customer concentration, capacity expansion, and margin trajectory.
search_queries: "China plus one" API supplier India public company
"drug master file" specialty API manufacturer listed
supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: These companies may be classified as commodity pharma or chemicals despite behaving more like sticky specialty suppliers with regulatory switching costs.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: Approved drug formulations often depend on specific API sources embedded in regulatory filings, making supplier changes costly, slow, and operationally disruptive.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: A single large domestic rolling facility outage can reveal hidden customer dependency and create opportunities for alternate qualified suppliers, toll processors, recyclers, and specialty aluminum producers.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Search USD 300M-10B metals processors, recyclers, and specialty aluminum companies; include private suppliers only as dependency evidence, not investable candidates.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Automotive aluminum sheet and specialty rolling capacity
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Map automaker supplier disclosures, plant-level capacity, qualification status, and substitute availability for aluminum sheet, body panels, battery enclosures, and EV lightweighting materials.
search_queries: "automotive aluminum sheet" supplier Ford Lucid Novelis competitor
"Novelis" Oswego plant outage alternate supplier listed
"automotive body sheet" aluminum qualified supplier public company
supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: The immediate headline is an automaker production issue, but the deeper research target is the small set of qualified specialty rolling assets and the suppliers that can absorb emergency demand.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: EVs and lightweight vehicles depend on qualified aluminum sheet and rolling capacity; outages at concentrated facilities can disrupt automaker supply chains.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: The most investable scarcity may sit upstream of reactor ownership: enrichment, HALEU, uranium conversion, forgings/components, licensing, and qualified engineering capacity rather than only utilities or reactor developers.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Prioritize USD 500M-10B nuclear fuel-cycle and component suppliers; treat pre-revenue reactor developers as speculative unless supported by licensing, funding, and customer contracts.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Nuclear fuel cycle, HALEU enrichment, reactor components, and project execution
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Use large nuclear names as references, then search for niche enrichment, component, valve, instrumentation, EPC, and certification-heavy suppliers with direct nuclear qualification evidence.
search_queries: "data center" nuclear power fuel supply HALEU
supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: Public narratives often emphasize SMRs or utilities; smaller second-order beneficiaries may sit in the regulated supply base that every nuclear project must use.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: AI data centers and electrification increase interest in reliable baseload and clean firm power, while nuclear deployment depends on regulated fuel, enrichment, specialized components, and EPC capacity.

demand_drivers: AI data-center buildout increasing demand for high-reliability passive components, advanced substrates, power delivery, thermal management, and grid infrastructure.
Electrification and data-center power demand increasing pressure on grid equipment, low-voltage components, backup power, and baseload power supply chains.
Critical-minerals processing demand from copper, nickel, batteries, and fertilizers creating sensitivity to sulphur and sulphuric-acid disruptions.
Healthcare supply-chain diversification away from China increasing demand for sticky, regulated, niche API suppliers in India and other non-China geographies.
Automotive lightweighting and EV supply chains creating vulnerability to concentrated aluminum rolling and specialty material suppliers.
Policy-driven nuclear revival and data-center power procurement increasing attention on uranium, enrichment, HALEU, reactor components, EPC, and regulated utility interfaces.

theme_map.public_market_search_strategy: Start with reference leaders only to define the demand shock, then search laterally for listed suppliers whose economics are controlled by qualification, purity, certification, capacity, route access, or customer lock-in. Prioritize USD 300M-10B market-cap companies when possible; include larger firms only when exposure is unusually pure, and micro-caps only as speculative-shadow candidates. For each node, search filings, capacity announcements, customer certifications, regulatory approvals, trade-flow data, and segment-level margin changes before moving to Layer 1B company screening.
supply_side_constraints: Long qualification cycles and customer re-validation requirements in regulated pharma API supply chains.
High-end MLCC manufacturing constraints where only a small number of companies can mass-produce the narrow band of parts needed for AI servers.
Advanced glass / T-glass process know-how and weaving-tolerance constraints for AI-related substrates and high-speed electronics.
Sulphur and sulphuric-acid trade-route disruptions affecting copper SX-EW, Indonesian HPAL nickel, and fertilizer supply chains.
Single-plant or regionally concentrated aluminum rolling capacity creating downstream auto production risk.
Nuclear licensing, fuel enrichment, HALEU availability, specialized component manufacturing, and project-execution bottlenecks.
